record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Directly measure the polarized gluon distribution ΔG(x,Q²) in the nucleon and determine gross features of its shape. Indirect estimates can use the Q² dependence of the quark helicity distribution Δq(x,Q²) through renormalization group evolution, but the open question is to determine ΔG via direct probes such as photon-gluon fusion in charm, two-jet, or pion-pair production, or QCD Compton production of high-transverse-momentum photons or jets.

evidence.quote: A direct measurement of the polarized gluon distribution in the nucleon is probably the highest priority for QCD spin physics.
Further refinement of the indirect method will improve our knowledge of ΔG, but direct measurement is essential to determine gross features of its shape.
The basic mechanism is photon-gluon fusion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a longitudinally polarized nucleon (proton or neutron). Within perturbative QCD in a given factorization scheme, the spin structure of the nucleon at scale Q² admits a decomposition involving the polarized gluon distribution ΔG(x, Q²) = ∫₀¹ [g₊(x,Q²) − g₋(x,Q²)] giving the difference between the number densities of gluons with helicity parallel and antiparallel to the nucleon helicity, carrying longitudinal momentum fraction x.

Problem: Determine ΔG(x, Q²) directly (not merely through scaling violations of the polarized quark singlet distribution Δq(x,Q²) under DGLAP evolution) for the nucleon, by exploiting hard processes in which gluons enter at leading order, such as:
(a) photon–gluon fusion γ*g → q q̄ in polarized lepton–nucleon scattering, in particular open-charm production (γ*g → c c̄) and high-pT hadron-pair (e.g. two-jet or pion-pair) production;
(b) QCD Compton scattering qg → qγ or qg → qg in polarized proton–proton collisions, yielding high transverse-momentum prompt photons or jets.

Specifically, measure the longitudinal double-spin asymmetries in these channels and from them extract both the magnitude and the gross x-shape (including the sign, the position of any node, and the first moment ΔG(Q²) = ∫₀¹ ΔG(x,Q²) dx) of the polarized gluon distribution over a wide range of x at perturbative Q².
artifact.category_tag: polarized parton distributions / QCD spin physics
artifact.status_search_result: Direct measurements have been performed since 2002 by COMPASS (open charm and high-pT hadron pairs in polarized DIS) and by RHIC experiments STAR and PHENIX (inclusive jets, dijets, and prompt photons in polarized pp collisions). Global QCD analyses including these data find evidence for a positive ΔG(x,Q²) at x ≳ 0.05 with a non-zero first moment, but the low-x behavior and overall sign/shape are still not pinned down; the program is ongoing and is a key goal of the future Electron-Ion Collider.

status_evidence.title: Direct Measurement of the Gluon Polarisation in the Nucleon via Charmed Meson Production (COMPASS)
status_evidence.snippet: COMPASS direct measurement of ΔG/G via open-charm photon-gluon fusion in polarized muon-nucleon scattering.
status_evidence.claim: Direct measurements of ΔG via photon-gluon fusion in charm production have been carried out.

status_evidence.title: On the resolution of the sign of gluon polarization in the proton
status_evidence.snippet: Negative-ΔG solutions are disfavored by Higgs production constraints when combined with lattice QCD; sign and shape remain under active study.
status_evidence.claim: The sign and shape of ΔG(x) are not fully settled as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: Gluon Helicity Distribution from Longitudinally Polarized Proton Collisions at STAR
status_evidence.snippet: STAR inclusive-jet and dijet ALL measurements at √s=200 and 510 GeV constrain ΔG, indicating non-zero gluon polarization for x>0.05.
status_evidence.claim: RHIC jet/dijet ALL data provide direct constraints on ΔG, showing evidence of non-zero gluon polarization at moderate x.
